extracted.intended_audience: journalists, stakeholders, and the general public interested in USCIS actions
extracted.subtask_description: Writing short, factual news releases for a federal agency (USCIS) announcing investigations, arrests, legal outcomes, or agency involvement; each release follows a consistent headline-date-body pattern and provides specific factual detail. These are meant for media distribution and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, action-focused headline
rubrics_metrics.description: A short title that summarizes the principal action or outcome (e.g., 'USCIS Efforts Lead to Two Guilty Pleas in H-1B Fraud Conspiracy Case').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active phrasing that highlights the actor (USCIS or subject) and the result (guilty pleas, found guilty, arrested). Avoid vague headlines; be specific about the case or outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: Each release displays the publication date immediately under the headline (e.g., 'April 23, 2026').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include an unambiguous month-day-year date near the top so readers and archives can place the item in time. Do not omit the date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate agency attribution and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead sentence names U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and states its role in the event (e.g., 'U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services’ fraud detection efforts resulted in the guilty pleas...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with the agency's involvement and the concrete result; this orients readers and establishes the source and responsibility for the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph summarizes key facts and result
rubrics_metrics.description: The first paragraph concisely states what happened and the principal result of USCIS activity (investigation led to indictment, arrest, guilty plea, denaturalization, sentencing, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the lead tightly focused on who did what to whom and the outcome. Avoid long background detail in the lead; reserve it for subsequent paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of individuals with specific descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases identify named individuals with age and relevant descriptors (e.g., 'Sampath Rajidi, 51', 'a native of Nigeria', 'a lawful permanent resident from South Korea').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full names and age; add nationality, residency status, or other concise identifiers when relevant to immigration context. Avoid speculative or unverified personal details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of legal status, charges, or proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate the legal action or status (e.g., 'guilty pleas to conspiracy to commit visa fraud', 'indicted', 'denaturalized', 'sentenced to 30 months in prison').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise legal terminology (indicted, pleaded guilty, convicted, denaturalized, sentenced) and, where appropriate, cite the charging authority (U.S. Attorney, federal jury, Department of Justice). Avoid ambiguous language about outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and jurisdictional specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: State the location or court/jurisdiction where the action occurred (e.g., 'charged in Los Angeles', 'in Texas', 'in North Carolina').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include city, state, or jurisdiction to give context about where enforcement or prosecution took place. Do not leave geographic context unspecified when it is material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of agency cooperation with other authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate collaboration with other agencies or offices (e.g., 'U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced', 'helped investigate... filed by the U.S. Department of Justice').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge partner agencies and their roles to reflect multi-agency investigations; name the other agency or office when publicly announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise, factual, non-editorial tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases are written as factual summaries without opinion or advocacy (e.g., 'USCIS provided pivotal assistance to the investigation that led to...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain neutral, reportorial voice; avoid sensational language, editorializing, or unconfirmed allegations. Stick to verifiable facts and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity about agency function or program involved
rubrics_metrics.description: When relevant, identify the specific USCIS function or program involved (e.g., 'fraud detection efforts', 'played a key role in the investigation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention the program, unit, or functional activity that led to the action to clarify how USCIS contributed. Be specific rather than generic when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide archival and subscription information on release listings
rubrics_metrics.description: The release index notes that releases are searchable by topic and date and points users to an 'Archive' for material older than three years; the page also offers subscription/RSS options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On listings pages, include metadata filters (topic/date), an archive policy for older material, and subscription/RSS links so media and the public can track releases. For individual releases, ensure metadata (date, topic tags) is present to support searchability.
